messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 5-kg (11-lb) weight gain and hair loss over the past 4 months. Menarche occurred at the age of 12 years and menses occurred at irregular intervals until she stopped having periods 2 months ago. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 82 kg (180 lb); BMI is 30 kg/m2. Physical examination shows a receding hairline and hair loss over the vertex of the head. Serum studies show:
Thyroid-stimulating hormone 2 μU/mL
Luteinizing hormone 32 mIU/mL
Prolactin 11 ng/mL
Urine pregnancy test is negative. Withdrawal bleeding occurs after a progestin challenge test. The most likely cause of amenorrhea in this patient is an increase in production of which of the following hormones?"

Options:
A. Progesterone in corpus luteum
B. Androgens in the adrenal gland
C. Estrogen in adipose tissue
D. Follicle stimulating hormone in the adenohypophysis
E. Dopamine in the hypothalamus

Correct answer: C. Estrogen in adipose tissue

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is an endocrinology/reproductive physiology question about the hormonal cause of amenorrhea, with no psychiatric content and nothing DSM-5 can answer."}
